Android from the foundation · Puzzle 12 of 15

Starting an app, cold, warm and hot

Opening an app can mean very different amounts of work, depending on whether its process and its screen still exist.

The problem

In puzzles 10 and 11, a new app process was forked from Zygote. But is a process forked every time you open an app? Sometimes the app opens instantly, sometimes it takes a second. What's the difference?

See it

Save this diagram as a GIF

The building block

Your app has one Application object per process: a place for setup the whole app needs, like opening a database. It's created right after the fork, and its callback Application.onCreate() runs before any Activity exists.

  • Cold start: no process yet. Fork from Zygote, create the Application, then create the first Activity.
  • Warm start: the process is still alive, but the Activity was destroyed (puzzle 3), for example because the user closed it, so it's created again.
  • Hot start: process and Activity are both alive, stopped in the background; system_server just brings the screen back to the front.

The analogy

Cold: build the house from the show house, move in, set up the room. Warm: the house stands, set up the room again. Hot: everything's ready, just open the curtains.

Check yourself

You put a slow database setup in Application.onCreate(). Which starts get slower?

Right. Application.onCreate() runs once per process, in a cold start, before any screen.

Not quite. Hot starts create nothing new. The Application only appears in a cold start.

Not quite. The Application is created once per process. Warm and hot starts reuse the living process.

The user comes back to your app a minute later and it opens instantly. Which kind of start was that likely?

Right. Hot starts reuse everything.

Not quite. A cold start does the most work: fork, Application, Activity.

What's the difference between a warm and a cold start?

Not quite. That's a hot start. A warm start creates the Activity again.

Right. Warm: process alive, screen rebuilt. Cold: everything from scratch.

Sources

  • Android Developers: App startup time
  • Android Developers: The activity lifecycle

What you now know

Cold start = fork Zygote, create your Application, then the first Activity. Warm = process alive, Activity created again. Hot = both alive, just brought to the front.
